chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If you recited al-Hamd upon a dead body seventy times and the soul was returned into it, that would not be surprising.

key_terms.الْحَمْدُ: Al-Hamd (The Praise), referring to Surah al-Fatihah, the 'Mother of the Book'
key_terms.مَيْتٍ: A dead body or deceased person

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of reciting Surah al-Hamd over the deceased?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the immense spiritual potency of Surah al-Fatihah, suggesting its recitation over the deceased is so powerful that it could theoretically restore life, thereby emphasizing its status as a cure and a source of divine mercy. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of the Quran not merely as text but as a living entity with tangible metaphysical effects on the soul and body. The emphasis on seventy recitations underscores the tradition of repetitive dhikr to amplify spiritual impact.

en.ammaar-muslim: [9/1558] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muawiya b. Ammar from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:
If al-Ḥamd were recited upon a dead body seventy times and the soul is returned into it (i.e. the dead body) that would not be surprising
